channel.title: Lecture Videos on MIT OpenCourseWare
channel.description: Recent content in Lecture Videos on MIT OpenCourseWare

item.title: Lecture 10: Phonology, Part 3
item.description: This video discusses language-specific rules for accent placement and other phonological features.

item.title: Lecture 11: Syntax, Part 1
item.description: This video introduces the fundamentals of how words are put together to form sentences.

item.title: Lecture 12: Syntax, Part 2
item.description: This video demonstrates how syntactic trees are used to show the structure of sentences.

item.title: Lecture 13: Syntax, Part 3
item.description: This video explains the relations between verbs and other constituents in a sentence.

item.title: Lecture 14: Syntax, Part 4
item.description: This video discusses how to use syntactic trees to analyze the grammar of sentences.

item.title: Lecture 15: Syntax, Part 5
item.description: This video discusses the acquisition of wh-movement and the extended projection principle.

item.title: Lecture 16: Syntax, Part 6
item.description: This video discusses the relations between heads and their complements in different languages.

item.title: Lecture 17: Syntax, Part 7, and Semantics, Part 1
item.description: This video concludes the discussion of syntax and begins the examination of semantics.

item.title: Lecture 18: Semantics, Part 2
item.description: This video discusses different kinds of ambiguity relating to quantifiers.

item.title: Lecture 19: Semantics, Part 3
item.description: This video discusses the semantics of quantifiers, including negative polarity items.

item.title: Lecture 2: Morphology, Part 1
item.description: This video provides a quick introduction to what morphology is.

item.title: Lecture 20: Semantics, Part 4
item.description: This video discusses the semantics of pronouns, anaphora, and binding theory.

item.title: Lecture 21: Semantics, Part 5
item.description: This video discusses semantic interpretations of sentences, particularly ones featuring ellipsis.

item.title: Lecture 22: Dialects
item.description: This video discusses differences in how languages deal with negatives, and explains some of the grammatical constraints that apply in African American English.

item.title: Lecture 23: Historical Linguistics
item.description: This video explains how semantic drift, recuttings, and sound changes over time cause languages to evolve and/or split into distinctly different languages.

item.title: Lecture 24: Endangered Languages
item.description: This video describes the efforts to revive the Wampanoag language, and the ways historical documents can be used to reconstruct the grammar of an extinct language.

item.title: Lecture 25: Language Acquisition
item.description: This video deals with how young children learn to understand and use language, as well as touching on the hypothesis that some aspects of grammar are innate.

item.title: Lecture 26: Signed Languages
item.description: This video deals with the linguistic aspects of signed rather than spoken languages.

item.title: Lecture 3: Morphology, Part 2
item.description: This video discusses the forms morphemes can take, and how morphemes are combined to make words.

item.title: Lecture 4: Morphology, Part 3
item.description: This video discusses how aspects of morphology vary from one language to another.

item.title: Lecture 5: Phonetics, Part 1
item.description: This video introduces the basic vocabulary used in discussing the sounds of speech.

item.title: Lecture 6: Phonetics, Part 2
item.description: This video presents more information on speech sounds, especially vowels.

item.title: Lecture 8: Phonology, Part 1
item.description: This video discusses rules by which morphemes are realized in pronunciation in various languages.

item.title: Lecture 9: Phonology, Part 2
item.description: This video discusses phonology and phonotactics in Japanese, English, and Arabic.
